spots.chart_note: Blue = falling water; darker blue = fastest water in a Prime, Great or Good window. Heights are depth at the dock. Dotted lines = 1 ft (getting shallow) and 0.5 ft (too shallow). Shaded columns = rain chance (darker = likelier; purple = storms). Bottom strip shows night, twilight and daylight.
spots.rules_text: Each window starts at 100 points: Prime 90+, Great 75+, Good 60+, Fair 40+, Poor below. Points lost: fall 1.5–2 ft −10, 1–1.5 ft −20, under 1 ft −45; under 1 ft deep during the fastest water −25, only after it −10; fastest water misses first light and sunset −10 (midday −20); wind 9–12 mph −5, 13–15 mph −10, over 15 mph −20; SSW–WSW wind −10 more; gusts 20+ −5; rain chance 20%+ −5, 50%+ −10; storms −20; cool water (under 60°) −10; choppy, murky water (wind averaging 13 mph or more over the window and the 12 h before) −10. Prime also needs a fall of 2 ft or more, fastest water at first light or sunset, at least 1 ft deep, wind 8 mph or less and not SSW–WSW, rain under 20%, no storms, clear water. Red tide nearby or cold water (under 55°) is Skip. Heights are depth at the dock; a window ends once it drops below 0.5 ft. Water temperature and red tide use the latest reading for every day. Fastest-water times are estimates.
